name: Grand Tourer, nobody at the wheel
description: Cognac and ivory nappa leather with contrast stitching, polished walnut burl, knurled metal, a wood-and-leather wheel and a hooded twin-dial cluster, and a tall screen in the centre of the dash for the radio. The same car as grand-tourer with no hands or arms on the wheel. A slim rear-view mirror hangs from the top edge of the frame.

source.size: 2K (2400x1792), downscaled to 1200x896; the 2K stills are kept outside the repo for the 1080p release
source.edits: The mirror came out two thirds of the way up the glass on a short stalk; tools/footage/mirror.py moved it to hang from the top edge with half of it in frame. The wheel's rim touched the windshield's bottom seal, so wheel.offset moves it 42 px down. The cabin edit re-rendered the glass with faint ghost lines, so the cockpit's keyed glass was copied into cabin.png. The painted needles (both at zero) were inpainted out of cabin.png so the composite can draw live ones (car.json dials). The three small gauges on the centre stack and the burl panel above them were replaced by one tall screen (the screen edit below, made on the 2K cabin; only the changed stack region was pasted into cabin.png and cockpit.png, behind the hand), so the radio has a place on the dash; the water temperature moved to the cluster's centre display (car.json screens).
source.cockpit: Photograph from the driver's seat of a modern luxury grand touring car, unbranded, camera at the driver's eye position looking STRAIGHT AHEAD, perfectly square to the car: the steering wheel hub exactly at the horizontal centre of the frame, the windshield head-on and symmetric, the left A-pillar at the far left edge and the right A-pillar at the far right edge, a sliver of the driver's door mirror at the far left. The windshield is wide and tall and the dashboard sits low, so the glass fills most of the upper frame and the A-pillars are slim. The rear-view mirror is a small, slim mirror with a thin dark bezel, hanging very high at the top centre-right of the frame, so high that the top edge of the frame cuts it off and only its lower half is visible; it hangs from the headliner on a short thin stalk, with NO overhead console, NO sensor housing, NO map lights and NO camera pod around it, and the headliner above the glass is a thin strip of dark suede. Both hands hold the wheel at 9 and 3 o'clock, wheel centred, forearms running down and out of the bottom of the frame. The whole steering wheel rim is one smooth, continuous, perfectly round circle; the top of the rim sits a little below the bottom edge of the windshield, fully in front of the dark instrument binnacle, not touching the glass. The interior is rich, tasteful and sporting, in the manner of a hand-built British or Italian grand tourer: the dashboard top is deep cognac-brown nappa leather with hand stitching in ivory thread, the lower dash and the door panel are ivory-white nappa leather with cognac piping, a wide band of polished walnut burl veneer with a deep mirror gloss runs across the dash face and along the door top, the vent bezels, the switchgear and the trim rings are knurled bright metal, and the three-spoke steering wheel has a rim of polished walnut burl at the top and bottom and perforated cognac nappa leather at the sides where the hands hold it, with a brushed metal spoke centre. Behind the wheel, under a slim leather hood, a bright backlit analogue instrument cluster with crisp white numerals and tick marks, glowing white needles and an amber accent ring, clearly legible. Bright early-afternoon daylight pours through the windshield from ahead-right, lighting the dash top with soft specular highlights on the leather and the wood, glinting on the metal trim and casting a soft A-pillar shadow, so every material reads clearly. No logos, no badges, no brand marks, no screens with content. The ENTIRE windshield, the side windows and the glass of every mirror are filled with a perfectly flat, uniform, pure chroma-key green (#00FF00) with no reflections, no gradient and no scenery, and nothing in the cabin reflects any green. 26 mm lens, level horizon, no camera rotation. Frame tall (4:3) so there is extra room below the wheel for the forearms.
source.mirrorEdit: Edit this photograph. Move the rear-view mirror straight up until it hangs from the very top edge of the frame, so that the top edge of the frame cuts through the mirror and only the lower half of the mirror is visible, and make the mirror about 20 percent smaller. Its glass stays a perfectly flat, uniform, pure chroma-key green (#00FF00) with a thin dark bezel. Remove the dark sensor housing and the dark shaded band on the windshield glass above and around the mirror, so the windshield there is the same flat pure green as the rest; the headliner stays the same thin strip of dark suede along the top. Keep everything else exactly as it is, pixel for pixel. (The model removed the housing but left the mirror where it was; mirror.py moved it.)
source.cabin: Edit this image. Remove the steering wheel and the driver's hands and arms completely, and show what is behind them: the steering column and stalk housing, the full backlit instrument cluster under its leather hood, the lower dashboard, the knee bolster and the driver's lap and seat, all in the same materials and lighting. Keep everything else, including the flat pure green windshield, side window and mirror glass, the rear-view mirror at the top edge, the dash, wood, leather, metal trim, vents and A-pillars, exactly as it is, pixel for pixel. Same framing, same 4:3 size.
source.screenEdit: Edit this photograph of a luxury car's dashboard. On the right half of the dashboard, replace two things with ONE tall built-in display screen: the polished walnut burl panel on the dashboard face between the two right-hand round air vents, and the curved bright-metal console panel below it that holds three small round gauges. The three small round gauges are removed completely. The new screen is a single upright rectangle with softly rounded corners, a little taller than it is wide: its left edge sits just right of the centre air vent, its right edge just left of the far right air vent, its top edge a little below the stitched leather dashboard top, and its bottom edge just above the wood panel with the small badge on the lower console. It is set flush into the walnut and framed with a thin bezel of polished bright metal, matching the knurled metal rings of the air vents. The screen is switched off: deep black glossy glass, with only a faint, soft, even sheen from the daylight coming through the windshield across its upper left corner. No content on it, no text, no icons, no logos, no buttons, no reflections of objects. The walnut and leather around the screen continue naturally up to its bezel. Keep everything else exactly as it is, pixel for pixel: both right-hand air vents and their metal rings, the instrument cluster, the stitched leather dashboard top, the burl veneer, the chrome trim, the lower console with its badge and the head unit buttons below it, the door, the seat, the flat pure green windshield, side window and mirror glass, the same framing, the same light, the same 4:3 size.
source.mirrors: 18 Oct 2026: no generated view in any mirror. The door mirror's glass was painted over in cockpit.png and cabin.png as the back of its own dark housing (the shell beside the glass cloned across it, with a soft vertical gradient), so its box keys nothing and only the housing shows; the originals are kept outside the repo (docs/sample-videos/cars-src/grand-tourer/*-1200-mirror-glass.png). The rear-view keeps its green glass: composite.sh fills it with dark auto-dimmed glass, and the app draws the Alerts bell on it.
source.gloves: 27 Oct 2026: this car is grand-tourer with the driver's hands and forearms removed (an image edit of cockpit.png that paints the rim at 9 and 3 and the lap; docs/sample-videos/cars-src/grand-tourer/no-hands/, take b; prompt in no-hands.prompt.txt). tools/footage/handpaste.py pasted only the old hands region of the edit into cockpit.png; hands-mask.png is all black, which tells wheel.py there are no hands, so the matte is the wheel's disc only. Everything else is a copy of cars/grand-tourer.
